BLOCKER: `scripts/dev/residency_gate.py` returns `0 if a.report else 1` on a block: `--report` silently downgrades a blocking violation to exit 0. AC says `--report` is non-fatal only in the sense it must not *add* failure; here it removes it and neuters the CI gate (which also passes no --report, but any operator/CI use of --report disables enforcement).

Neither `core.packaging.validate_residency` nor Go `Validate` ever emits `RESIDENCY_MISSING_GROUP:egress`; Python even `continue`s past it. AC requires all six groups populated — an empty/missing `egress` block passes both validators.

Conformance fixture set (AC5) is incomplete: no cases for missing `home_region`, `backup`/`kms` region outside allowed, invalid `kms.provider`, unreadable/missing profile, or toolchain/validator-unavailable. The "one fixture set drives both validators identically" requirement is only partially met.
MAJOR: Python `validate_residency` appends `RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME` twice for an empty home (once unconditionally, once in the dead `if not home or not re.match(...)` branch whose two arms are identical) — duplicated/non-deterministic error codes undermine the "stable error codes" contract and parity comparisons.

Go `Validate` treats a profile with empty `ID` or empty `allowed_regions` as `RESIDENCY_PROFILE_UNREADABLE`; Python only checks file existence/readability. If any `config/residency-profiles/*.json` lacks an `id` field, the two validators disagree and the gate hard-blocks on "parity failure" at exit 2.

Python flags `RESIDENCY_REGION_NOT_ALLOWED` whenever the profile is unreadable/empty (spurious `not sec_allowed <= allowed`), producing noisy multi-error output that differs from Go's behavior on the same input.

`hard = {UNKNOWN_HOME, PROFILE_UNREADABLE, SCHEMA_VERSION}` matches raw codes, so `RESIDENCY_MISSING_GROUP:home_region` and `RESIDENCY_INVALID_FIELD:*` are warn-downgraded in warn mode — AC says warn may downgrade only policy violations; field/schema-class errors silently pass.

`packaging.build` swallows an unreadable manifest into `{"error": "RESIDENCY_MANIFEST_UNREADABLE"}` and still emits a "successful" build manifest; build integrity should fail loudly rather than embed an error blob.

Gate shells out to `go run` on every fast-tier precheck/CI run (compiles the module each time, 120s timeout); no prebuilt-binary reuse or toolchain version pin, risking slow and environment-dependent gates.
MINOR: `return 0 if a.report else 0` in the warn branch is dead code and signals confusion about the exit-code contract.
`config/residency-manifest.json` template carries `"template": true` and `notes` that flow into the built packaging manifest, polluting shipped artifacts.
Products override `products/<project>/residency-manifest.json` is not registered in store-registry.json with an owner, unlike the template.
`id-blocks.json` diff leaves a gap (1187–1189 unused, new session starts at 1190) and mixes unrelated allocator churn into this change.
Go `LoadProfile`/`LoadManifest` build paths with `fmt.Sprintf` and `strings.TrimRight(dir, "/\\")` instead of `filepath.Join` — works but fragile on Windows and for trailing separators.
NIT: `--profiles` Go default `"config/residency-profiles"` is cwd-relative and only correct when run from repo root.
`store-registry.json` allow-list adds scratch filenames (`residency_*_scratch.json`) that only exist because tests write into the repo instead of tmp; prefer tmp everywhere.
`residency_gate.py` warn message prints the full error list per run, which will grow the .jsonl quickly despite the rotation bound; consider truncating to counts + codes.
`_policy()` prints a BLOCK line but returns a dict that continues execution; clearer to exit 2 immediately on unreadable policy.
SUMMARY: Solid shape overall: Go validator as authority, profile-bounded rules, stable codes, warn-first rollout lever with expiry, and cross-language conformance scaffolding are the right architecture.

However the gate's `--report` exit-0 path is a real enforcement bypass, `egress` missing-group is never checked (AC violation), and the fixture/conformance coverage falls short of AC5's "every RESIDENCY_* error incl. schema/invalid-field/toolchain/profile".
Secondary risk: Python/Go divergence on profile parsing (`id` field, unreadable-profile error set) will manifest as flaky exit-2 parity blocks once real profiles vary.
